summary:
**AstroGuard: Astronaut Health Assessment and Guidance System**

AstroGuard is an interactive astronaut health assessment and guidance system developed to support astronauts in monitoring their physical and general well-being during space missions. The system integrates health data recording, interactive dashboards, historical analytics, an interactive human body explorer and an AI-assisted health guidance feature.

Astronauts can record health indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep duration and reported symptoms. AstroGuard visualizes these measurements through charts and provides understandable insights to help users identify changes in their health patterns. It also offers educational information about spaceflight hazards, explains their effects on different body systems and provides general recommendations for maintaining well-being.

By combining health monitoring, data visualization and AI-assisted guidance in one platform, AstroGuard addresses the challenges of understanding and monitoring astronaut health in space. It is important because early awareness of potential health concerns can support timely medical attention, encourage preventive health practices and improve astronauts' well-being during long-duration space missions.
details:
1. What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

AstroGuard is an interactive web-based astronaut health assessment and guidance system designed to help astronauts monitor their physical and general well-being during space missions.

The system allows users to manually enter health measurements, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), blood pressure, body temperature, respiratory rate and sleep duration. Users can also report symptoms, stress levels and fatigue through an interactive assessment interface.

The recorded information is displayed on a centralized dashboard, where users can review their latest health measurements and monitoring status. Historical analytics provide charts to visualize changes in health indicators over time. Additionally, the Interactive Human Body Explorer allows users to explore different body systems and understand how spaceflight conditions may affect them.

AstroGuard also incorporates an AI-assisted Health Assistant that provides explanations of recorded information, general health insights and educational answers about astronaut health. Other features include spaceflight hazard information, personalized health recommendations, activity tracking, assessment reminders and health reports.

2. What Are the Benefits?

AstroGuard offers several benefits:

  • Centralized Health Monitoring: Provides one platform for recording and reviewing multiple health indicators.
  • Improved Health Awareness: Helps astronauts understand their health measurements through visualizations and explanations.
  • Historical Data Analysis: Allows users to identify changes and patterns in their health records over time.
  • Accessible Health Education: Explains how spaceflight hazards affect different body systems.
  • AI-Assisted Guidance: Provides understandable health insights and general recommendations.
  • Consistent Health Management: Encourages regular assessments through reminders, progress tracking and gamification.

3. What Is the Intended Impact?

The intended impact of AstroGuard is to improve astronaut health awareness and support better health management throughout space missions. By making health information easier to understand, the system encourages astronauts to monitor their conditions regularly and pay attention to potential health concerns.

It also aims to support communication between astronauts and medical professionals by organizing health records into accessible summaries. In the long term, AstroGuard could serve as a foundation for more advanced astronaut health monitoring systems integrated with wearable devices and real-time health data sources.

4. Tools, Programming Languages and Software Used

AstroGuard was developed as a web-based application using the following technologies:

  • HTML: Structures the web application and its content.
  • CSS: Designs the interface, layouts, visual elements and responsive presentation.
  • JavaScript: Implements application logic, user interactions and data processing.
  • React.js: Develops reusable components and manages interactive user interfaces.
  • Vite: Provides the development environment and frontend build process.
  • Node.js: Supports backend functionality and server-side operations.
  • NASA DONKI API: Integrates space weather information, including solar flare and other space weather event data, to provide additional context about space-related hazards.
  • Local Storage: Stores user assessment records and application data locally for future reference.
  • Chart Visualization Libraries: Display historical health measurements and trends through interactive charts.
  • AI Development Tools: ChatGPT (GPT) and Claude were used as AI-assisted development tools to support brainstorming, generating and refining code, debugging technical issues, explaining programming concepts and improving the overall system implementation.

The application was also deployed using a web hosting platform to make it accessible beyond the local development environment.

5. How Is the Project Creative and Innovative?

AstroGuard combines several concepts into one astronaut-focused health platform rather than functioning as a basic health data recording application.

Its creativity comes from the integration of an interactive human body explorer, health analytics, AI-assisted explanations, spaceflight hazard education and gamification. Instead of presenting health measurements as isolated numbers, the system connects them with relevant body systems and spaceflight conditions to provide a more understandable experience.

The AI Health Assistant further improves accessibility by allowing users to explore health-related questions using natural language. Gamification elements, including health points, assessment streaks and activity progress, encourage consistent engagement with health monitoring.

6. What Factors Did the Team Consider?

During development, the team considered several important factors:

  • User Experience: The interface should be intuitive, organized and easy to navigate.
  • Accuracy and Reliability: Health information and recommendations should be presented responsibly and should not be treated as medical diagnoses.
  • Space Environment: Features should address relevant challenges such as microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation and limited medical access.
  • Data Management: Health records should be organized and accessible for historical review.
  • Accessibility: Information should be presented using understandable explanations, visual indicators and charts.
  • Scalability: The system should allow future integration with wearable health devices and additional external data sources.
  • Privacy and Security: Personal health information should be handled carefully and protected against unauthorized access.
  • Technical Feasibility: The selected technologies should support the team's development capabilities, available resources and project timeline.

Overall, AstroGuard aims to transform astronaut health information into accessible, understandable and actionable insights while supporting health awareness and responsible medical decision-making during space exploration.

AstroGuard – Installation & User Guide

1. Introduction

AstroGuard is a space-health monitoring prototype designed to help astronauts monitor their health conditions during space missions. The system provides health assessments, health recommendations, and space-weather information to support astronaut well-being.

This guide explains how to install, configure, and use the AstroGuard prototype.

2. System Requirements

Before running AstroGuard, ensure that you have installed:

  • Node.js (LTS version)
  • npm (Node Package Manager)
  • Visual Studio Code (recommended)
  • A modern web browser (Google Chrome recommended)
  • Internet connection

3. Installation Guide

Step 1: Download the Project

  1. Download the AstroGuard project from GitHub.
  2. Extract the downloaded ZIP file.
  3. Open the extracted project folder using Visual Studio Code.

Step 2: Install Dependencies

  1. Open the terminal in Visual Studio Code.
  2. Navigate to the project directory.
  3. Run the following command: npm install

Wait until all required dependencies have been installed.

4. NASA API Configuration

AstroGuard integrates NASA's API to retrieve space-weather information through NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information).

Users need to configure their own NASA API key before accessing the space-weather features.

Step 1: Obtain a NASA API Key

  1. Visit https://api.nasa.gov/
  2. Find the API Key registration section.
  3. Enter your details to request an API key.
  4. Copy the generated API key.

Step 2: Configure the API Key

  1. Open the AstroGuard project folder.
  2. Locate the .env.example file in the project root directory.
  3. Create a copy of the file and rename it to .env.
  4. Open the .env file.
  5. Locate the NASA API key configuration.

Insert your API key as follows:

NASA_API_KEY=YOUR_NASA_API_KEY

Replace YOUR_NASA_API_KEY with your actual NASA API key.

Important: Keep your API key inside the backend .env file. Do not place it in frontend source code or share it publicly.

5. Running AstroGuard

AstroGuard requires both the backend and frontend servers to run.

Step 1: Start the Backend Server

  1. Open a terminal in Visual Studio Code.
  2. Run: npm.cmd run server

The Node.js backend will start and handle requests to NASA DONKI.

Step 2: Start the Frontend Server

  1. Open another terminal.
  2. Run: npm.cmd run dev
  3. Wait for Vite to display the local development address.
  4. Open the address in your web browser.
